title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: What Actually Makes People More Productive with Adrian Espes [MVP]
description:
Buying Copilot licenses is easy; making people genuinely more effective with them is not. Microsoft MVP Adrian Espes shares what he sees in real adoption projects: prompting habits, data protection, a pragmatic rollout path and why efficiency is a better goal than productivity. For IT leaders and adoption teams planning or rescuing a Microsoft 365 Copilot rollout.
In this episode
00:00 – Does Copilot make people more productive?03:32 – Adrian's path into Microsoft 36508:45 – Copilot compared with other AI tools20:14 – Prompting without being a prompt engineer32:56 – Data protection and governance38:25 – A 30-60-90 day rollout roadmap48:41 – From productivity to efficiency55:07 – Rapid fire: hype, useful or future
Key takeaways
Copilot's biggest advantage is that it lives inside Microsoft 365 tools and works with your emails, meetings and documents under enterprise data protection.Good prompting is learned by practice: be clear about the goal, add context, and tailor prompt guidance to each department.Before rollout, decide whether free Copilot Chat is enough, review tenant settings such as Anthropic models under GDPR, and talk about efficiency rather than productivity.
Worth quoting
“when we use, Microsoft co-pilot with an enterprise account, we are protected, uh, with a Microsoft EDP enterprise data protection.” – Adrian Espes (34:35)
“And my recommendation is try the Microsoft 365 Copilot chat, the free version, the free version.” – Adrian Espes (42:19)
